text: GPO's official machine-readable (XML) annual CFR bulk data does not extend earlier than 2000.
notes: Guide is internally inconsistent: Sec. 1.1 says XML from 2007 (EE2), Sec. 1.2 says from 2000 (EE4). Either way, pre-2000 annual CFR is not available as GPO XML. FDsys-era doc; current govinfo bulk listing not checked (unreachable).

text: GPO's annual CFR XML start year is stated inconsistently (2007 vs 2000) within GPO's own CFR XML user guide.
notes: Internal conflict in one primary document; resolve by listing https://www.govinfo.gov/bulkdata/CFR/ (unreachable here).

text: Only the PDF and text renditions of the CFR on GPO's system carry official legal status; the XML bulk files do not.
notes: FDsys-era statement; GPO may have since changed status. Implies a product citing pre-2017 regs should cite/anchor to the official PDF/text annual edition.

text: GPO's annual-CFR XML contains conversion anomalies because it was derived from SGML and typesetting codes and was not cleaned to match its schema.
notes: Data-quality risk for any pipeline built on GPO CFR XML; parsing/QA labor is part of the real moat.

text: The eCFR is an unofficial editorial compilation of the CFR that OFR can update as often as daily.
notes: GPO/OFR guide plus independent developer repo agree.

text: eCFR point-in-time versions are available only from January 3, 2017 onward.
notes: Two independent non-publisher sources (CMS dev wiki: 'only can go back to 2017'; cfr-mcp docstring: 'must be 2017-01-03 or later'). Official eCFR reader aid (ES37) was unreachable. Matches July 2026 lead (~Jan 2017).

text: GPO's bulk e-CFR XML began in 2015 and the bulk repository serves only the most recent eCFR snapshot, not historical versions.
notes: FDsys-era guide; historical eCFR versions must instead be pulled via the eCFR versioner API (post-2017 only).

text: The eCFR API can return CFR text as it stood on a specified date (YYYY-MM-DD) and publishes no rate limit or API key requirement.
notes: Single individual-developer source; official eCFR API docs unreachable.

text: eCFR point-in-time data for Title 38 has required manual correction patches, including fixes for wrong amendment dates.
notes: Eight Title 38 patch folders exist (incl. 003-fix-bad-amendment-date, 004/005/008 amddate fixes). Repo owner appears to be the FR/eCFR developer (meta references 'federal-register-2-0') but not independently verified. One patch (003) corrects an editorial date error in the 2021-02-09 and 2021-02-10 Title 38 versions. Implies even post-2017 day-level data needs validation.

text: GPO offers a free official govinfo API for programmatic access, requiring an api.data.gov key and capped at 36,000 requests per hour.
notes: Primary. Per-collection start years (CFR 1996/97, FR 1936/1994) not stated on page.

text: GPO's link service retrieves CFR sections by four-digit year, i.e., at annual-edition granularity rather than day-level.
notes: Earliest year available via link service not stated. Title 38 annual edition is (per general knowledge, unverified here) revised as of July 1 each year.

text: GPO's Federal Register XML begins in 2000; the 1994-1999 electronic Federal Register had not been converted to XML as of the guide.
notes: FDsys-era; may have been converted since. Pre-2000 FR exists as PDF/OCR (see EC27 lead).

text: Reconstructing whole regulation versions from Federal Register final rules is technically feasible but requires manual patching of amendment-instruction (AMDPAR) parsing errors.
notes: Demonstrated by eRegs parser docs. Directly relevant: pre-2017 point-in-time 38 CFR would require this kind of reconstruction from annual editions + FR.

text: The main open-source tool for building regulation version histories from final rules (eregs/regulations-parser) was archived and made read-only on April 4, 2023.
notes: No maintained open-source equivalent was identified in this run (gap, search budget exhausted).

text: U.S. government CFR/FR data carry no copyright restrictions on reuse, so raw regulatory text itself cannot be an exclusive data asset.
notes: EE8 is a fetch-tool summary (verbatim:false). Inference: any moat must come from reconstruction, versioning, QA and linkage, not from owning the text.

text: Free, machine-readable, day-level versions of 38 C.F.R. before 2017 are not available from government sources; pre-2017 versions must be assembled from annual editions plus Federal Register amendments.
notes: INFERENCE from EC1/EC6/EC7/EC12. Commercial availability (HeinOnline/Westlaw/Lexis) addressed only as leads (EC28-EC34).

text: VA publishes all BVA decisions as plain-text files indexed by per-year XML sitemaps at va.gov/vetappYY.
notes: Documented by Free Law Project code (Feb 2026); VA pages themselves unreachable in this run.

text: The public BVA decision corpus runs from 1992 to the present.
notes: Issue #873 (2024) said sitemaps covered 1992-2022; Feb 2026 code says 1992-present. Completeness per year not verified.

text: Published BVA decisions do not include veterans' names; the docket number serves as the identifier.
notes: Redaction implies decisions cannot be matched to a client's C-file by name; matching would need docket/citation numbers.

text: BVA decisions are classified as nonprecedential (each decision binds only the case decided).
notes: From scraper metadata; legal basis (38 C.F.R. 20.1303) not fetched. Limits value of BVA corpus as authority vs. as outcome/argument data.

text: VA's previous BVA decision search endpoint (index.va.gov) went dead around January 2024, and the replacement search requires a text query that Free Law Project considered unreliable for harvesting.
notes: Platform-change risk for anyone depending on VA-hosted decision search.

text: As of January 29, 2026, CourtListener's most recent BVA decision was dated October 30, 2021, a gap of over four years.
notes: Scraper rewrite PR #1822 merged 2026-02-27 (merge date from page metadata, not quoted). Whether CourtListener backfilled 2021-2026 is unverified.

text: Bulk harvesting of the BVA corpus is slow: VA serves large (15-20MB) sitemaps and text files without HTTP range support from slow servers.
notes: Operational cost, not a barrier; corpus of ~1M+ decisions (count not verified) would take sustained crawling.

text: CourtListener collects CAVC opinions from uscourts.cavc.gov via a scraper created in 2012 that looks back only four weeks, so its CAVC coverage is prospective from ~2012 unless backfilled from other sources.
notes: Pre-2012 CAVC coverage on CourtListener (e.g., via bulk reporter imports) not determined; CourtListener bulk/API terms unreachable (ES38).

text: A research corpus of BVA decisions from 2001-2018 exists, originating with the authors of arXiv 2106.10776 (ICAIL 2021 citation-recommendation paper) and distributed via Stanford RegLab/Google Drive.
notes: Two distinct repo owners (TUM Legal Tech; Pile of Law) but a single data origin. Decision count and license not stated (TUM README states no license).

text: The 2001-2018 BVA decisions are included in Pile of Law, a 256GB open legal corpus hosted on Hugging Face.
notes: Hugging Face dataset card (license/terms) unreachable. Freely available corpus means BVA text is not a moat.

text: The only openly annotated BVA argument-structure dataset found (LLT Lab VetClaims-JSON) is small: 50 PTSD decisions from 2013-2017 labeled by sentence rhetorical role.
notes: MIT license linked but not read. No CUE- or effective-date-specific annotated corpus was found (gap).
